answer: The tide design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. Decay keeps the economy honest: an identity that stops contributing loses its privileges, so bought or farmed reputation has a shelf life. The nebula turns sybils into a treadmill — the farm must keep all its clones working forever, and the moment it stops, they are worth nothing. That is the point of the lotus: cloning stops paying the moment each copy costs as much as the original.
